title: Hiring an Independent Real Estate Lawyer in Türkiye (Bar Association Check)
seoTitle: Hiring an Independent Real Estate Lawyer in Türkiye
metaDescription: Verify a Turkish property lawyer via the Bar Association (Baro), keep counsel independent of sellers, and review TAPU, Iskan, and legal fees.
quickAnswer: Foreign buyers should hire a Turkish real estate lawyer who has zero financial ties to the seller, developer, or sales agent. Before paying any deposit, verify the attorney's active license on the [Union of Turkish Bar Associations (TBB)](https://barobirlik.org.tr/AvukatArama) directory and request a written scope covering TAPU, Iskan, zoning, and debt checks.

body.text: Buying residential or commercial property in Türkiye involves binding land-registry filings, municipal checks, and notarized contracts written in Turkish. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders coordinate inspection trips, city logistics, and independent introductions on a transparent, client-paid flat fee ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions."). We never partner with developers or brokerage agencies, and we do not practice law or provide tax advice; all title (TAPU), contract, and tax decisions belong strictly to licensed Turkish attorneys, SMMM accountants, and official authorities.
How do you verify a Turkish lawyer's Bar Association (Baro) license?

Every licensed attorney practicing in Türkiye must hold active registration with a provincial Bar Association (Baro) and appear on the public [TBB Baro Levhası lookup](https://barobirlik.org.tr/AvukatArama). To verify a lawyer, ask for their full Turkish legal name, provincial bar (such as Istanbul or Antalya), and Baro registration number (sicil numarası), then confirm the active listing directly.

You can search nationwide via TBB or filter by province—for instance, using the [Istanbul Bar Association roster](https://www.barobirlik.org.tr/LevhaIFrame/34) or the [Antalya Bar Association roster](https://barobirlik.org.tr/AvukatArama/7). Be cautious of "legal consultants" or property-sales representatives who offer to draft contracts without an active Avukat license. Only a registered Turkish attorney can legally represent you in court or provide formal Turkish legal counsel under the Attorneyship Law.
Why must your property lawyer be 100% independent of the seller or agent?

A lawyer recommended by a developer or sales agency faces an immediate conflict of interest because their repeat referrals depend on closing deals quickly rather than flagging defects. Independent counsel paid directly by the buyer has a sole fiduciary duty to protect your deposit, negotiate penalty clauses, and advise you to walk away if records fail due diligence.

In many foreign-buyer transactions, sales offices present pre-printed reservation forms with non-refundable deposit terms or incomplete delivery guarantees. An independent real estate lawyer reviews the Turkish-language contract before you sign anything, verifies that the signatory has valid corporate authority to sell, and checks whether funds are routed to the actual legal owner rather than an intermediary.
What due diligence (TAPU, Iskan, zoning, debt checks) is included?

Comprehensive legal due diligence verifies both the land registry record at the [General Directorate of Land Registry and Cadastre (TKGM)](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/e-hizmetler/sik-kullanilanlar/web-tapu) and the physical compliance file at the local district municipality. Your attorney should issue a written due diligence report before any binding transfer or large payment occurs.

items: TAPU Encumbrances: Check for mortgages (ipotek), court seizures (haciz), tax liens, usufruct rights, or third-party annotations (şerh) via TKGM records.
Title Classification: Confirm whether the deed is full condominium ownership (kat mülkiyeti), construction servitude (kat irtifakı), or raw land share (arsa payı).
Iskan & Architectural Match: Verify the municipal occupancy permit (yapı kullanma izin belgesi) and confirm the physical unit matches the approved floor plan.
Zoning & Foreign-Buyer Eligibility: Confirm the parcel sits outside military-restricted zones and complies with current neighborhood residency or foreign-ownership caps.
Municipal & Site Debts: Check for unpaid property tax (emlak vergisi) at the municipality and overdue building maintenance fees (aidat) with site management.

body.text: What are typical legal fees for a residential purchase?

Independent Turkish real estate lawyers typically quote either a flat fee or a small percentage of the purchase price, depending on transaction complexity, language requirements, and whether power of attorney is used. Standard residential conveyancing commonly ranges from 1% to 1.5% of the property value (or a flat fee starting around €1,500–€3,500 for straightforward resales), excluding statutory disbursements.

faq.q: Can a Turkish real estate lawyer complete the TAPU transfer using Power of Attorney?
faq.a: Yes. Buyers can grant a narrowly scoped notarized Power of Attorney (vekaletname)—signed at a Turkish notary with a sworn translator or at a Turkish consulate abroad—authorizing the lawyer to sign TAPU transfer filings without granting unrestricted financial powers.

faq.q: Is a lawyer legally mandatory to buy property in Türkiye?
faq.a: Turkish law does not require a lawyer to attend a TAPU transfer, which is why many agents say one is unnecessary. However, because registry records, zoning files, and contracts are in Turkish, independent legal representation is essential to avoid hidden liens or unpermitted structures.

faq.q: Can I check a TAPU myself on Web Tapu before hiring a lawyer?
faq.a: Only the current registered owner can log into [e-Devlet Web Tapu](https://www.turkiye.gov.tr/tkgm-web-tapu) to generate an official digital verification code (Tapu Kayıt Belgesi) for a prospective buyer or their attorney to inspect.

faq.q: Does the TBB Baro directory show if a lawyer speaks English?
faq.a: The TBB directory confirms active bar membership, registration number, and provincial bar affiliation. Language fluency and real-estate specialization should be verified directly during an initial video consultation and confirmed in your engagement letter.

faq.q: Should I pay a reservation deposit before my lawyer finishes due diligence?
faq.a: Avoid paying a non-refundable deposit before basic TAPU and seller-authority checks are complete. If a seller insists on a holding deposit, ask your independent lawyer to draft a short refund clause tied directly to clean due diligence results.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye recommend partner real estate agencies or law firms for a commission?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye is funded solely by client flat fees and never accepts commissions or referral kickbacks from developers, agencies, or law firms.
